exercises.title: Prototype risks 1 — name the risk
exercises.problemHtml:
Wiegers’ four prototyping risks: pressure to release the prototype, distraction by details, unrealistic performance expectations, investing excessive effort in prototypes. Name the risk in each story.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
Bốn rủi ro: áp lực phát hành prototype, sa đà chi tiết, kỳ vọng hiệu năng phi thực tế, đầu tư quá mức. Gọi tên rủi ro trong từng tình huống.

Yêu cầu

  • Trả lời mọi câu trong khung trả lời rồi bấm Nộp.
  • Đúng hết mới được Accepted; giải thích từng câu hiện sau khi nộp.

exercises.title: Prototype risks 2 — success factors
exercises.problemHtml:
Success factors: include prototyping tasks in the project plan; state each prototype’s purpose before building it and what will happen to it afterwards; plan to build multiple prototypes; create throwaways as quickly and cheaply as possible; don’t prototype requirements you already understand (except to explore design); use plausible data; don’t expect a prototype to replace written requirements.

Requirements

  • Answer every question in the answer panel, then press Submit.
  • All answers must be correct to get Accepted; the explanations appear after you submit.

exercises.title: Prototype risks 3 — write a prototype plan that avoids the traps
exercises.problemHtml:
ClinicCare: doctors are unsure how the new e-prescription screen should work, and IT doubts the national e-health API can answer within 3 seconds. Plan two prototypes. Write PLANS: an array of two objects { name, purpose, scope, futureUse, form, fate, timeboxDays, questions }:

  • scope: "mock-up" or "proof of concept"; futureUse: "throwaway" or "evolutionary"; form: "paper" or "electronic".
  • fate: what happens afterwards — must be consistent with futureUse (a throwaway is discarded or archived, never released).
  • timeboxDays: a number ≤ 10 (avoid over-investing).
  • questions: at least 3 evaluation questions; the UI prototype must ask about missing functionality and error conditions.

Requirements

  • One prototype answers the UI question, the other the technical question.
exercises.problemHtmlVi:
ClinicCare: bác sĩ chưa rõ màn hình kê đơn điện tử; IT nghi API quốc gia không trả lời kịp 3 giây. Lập kế hoạch hai prototype với các trường như mô tả; số phận phải khớp với futureUse; timebox ≤ 10 ngày; ít nhất 3 câu hỏi đánh giá, prototype giao diện phải hỏi về chức năng thiếu và tình huống lỗi.

Yêu cầu

  • Một prototype trả lời câu hỏi giao diện, cái kia trả lời câu hỏi kỹ thuật.

examplesJson.output: { scope: 'mock-up', futureUse: 'throwaway', form: 'paper', fate: 'discard after updating the SRS', … }

hintsJson: Câu hỏi giao diện ⇒ mock-up giấy, throwaway; câu hỏi API ⇒ proof of concept điện tử.

starterCodeJson.name: plans.js

solutionCodeJson.name: plans.js
solutionCodeJson.code:
const PLANS = [
  {
    name: 'E-prescription screen mock-up',
    purpose: 'Clarify how doctors want to search medicines, set dosage and sign the prescription; find missing requirements.',
    scope: 'mock-up', futureUse: 'throwaway', form: 'paper',
    fate: 'Discard after the findings are written into the SRS; keep photos in the project archive.',
    timeboxDays: 3,
    questions: [
      'Which steps of writing a prescription are missing from these screens?',
      'What should happen when a medicine is out of stock or the dosage exceeds the limit (error conditions)?',
      'Are there any fields or functions here you would never use?',
      'Is the order of the screens logical for a busy consultation?',
    ],
  },
  {
    name: 'National e-health API spike',
    purpose: 'Check that sending one prescription through the national e-health API end to end returns within 3 seconds.',
    scope: 'proof of concept', futureUse: 'throwaway', form: 'electronic',
    fate: 'Discard the spike code; record the measured response times and the integration findings in the architecture notes.',
    timeboxDays: 5,
    questions: [
      'What is the 95th-percentile response time for 100 test submissions?',
      'Which error codes does the API return and how often?',
      'Does authentication work with our certificate?',
    ],
  },
];

exercises.solutionExplanationHtml: Two small, purpose-driven, time-boxed experiments: a throwaway paper mock-up for the uncertain screen and an electronic spike for the uncertain API. Their knowledge is kept; their artefacts are discarded.
